scenes.narration: Env Setup. Maven Project Structure (Part 1 of 2). In this video we review 5 key concepts you need to know for the certification.

scenes.question: What are the two types of repository areas in AEM's Maven project structure?
scenes.heading: Immutable and Mutable
scenes.body: AEM enforces a clear separation between two repository areas: Immutable (cannot be changed at runtime — `/apps`, `/libs`) and Mutable (can be changed at runtime — `/content`, `/conf`, `/var`, `/etc`). This separation is critical for AEMaaCS.

scenes.question: Which of the following repository paths is considered Immutable in AEM?
scenes.heading: /apps
scenes.body: `/apps` is an immutable repository path. It stores custom components, HTL scripts, clientlibs, and OSGi bundle overlays. It cannot be changed at runtime — all changes must go through the deployment pipeline.

scenes.question: Which of the following repository paths is considered Mutable in AEM?
scenes.heading: /content
scenes.body: `/content` is a mutable repository path. It holds site content (pages, assets) that can be created, edited, and published at runtime by authors. Other mutable paths include `/conf`, `/var`, and `/etc`.

scenes.question: What does /libs contain in the AEM repository?
scenes.heading: AEM platform code — the out-of-the-box components and libraries provided by Adobe
scenes.body: `/libs` contains AEM's own platform code — the out-of-the-box components, templates, and libraries provided by Adobe. This path is immutable and should never be modified directly. Custom overlays go in `/apps`.

scenes.question: Why should you never modify content directly under /libs?
scenes.heading: Because /libs is AEM's platform code — modifications are overwritten on AEM upgrades
scenes.body: You should never modify `/libs` because it contains Adobe's platform code. On AEM upgrades, `/libs` is overwritten, so any direct modifications would be lost. The correct approach is to create overlays in `/apps` — AEM's Sling resource merger picks up `/apps` first.
